label: Kimi K3.1 Pro
output:
Tolu, first of all, I’m sorry. That feeling of checking the portal full of confidence and seeing a completely different course is not something anybody should dismiss with “just be grateful.” You have every right to be disappointed.

And yes, you’re asking for somebody like me. I’m currently in Biology 100L in a federal university here in Lagos, but Medicine and Surgery was what I originally wanted. I wrote JAMB in 2025 and scored 251. I didn’t get Medicine; I was offered Biology. So I’m not speaking as somebody who has successfully transferred to MBBS o. I’m speaking as somebody who is inside Biology right now, still trying, and has asked my own level adviser plenty of questions.

Let me start with transfer, because that is the main thing confusing you.

**Transfer is not a myth, but it is definitely not automatic.** Kingsley saying it is something they use to console people is not true, at least not according to what we’ve been told in my own school. But favour saying “just read hard” is also too simple, because reading hard alone does not create space in Medicine.

My level adviser told us that, for my school, you need **at least a 4.5 CGPA out of 5.0 after 100L**, and **there must also be space in MBBS**. Those are two different conditions. Meeting the CGPA does not mean they must take you if there is no available space or if other people rank ahead of you.

She also said that last year, about six people were moved into Medicine from the **whole faculty**, not six people from Biology alone. She thinks more than 40 people applied. I’m saying “about” and “she thinks” because those were the figures she gave us, not an official published breakdown that I personally verified. Still, it should show you that transfer is possible without being something you should bank your whole future on.

There was another part people conveniently leave out: my adviser said you must also have met the requirements for Medicine in your original admission process, including the relevant JAMB and post-UTME cut-offs. That is why your 268, by itself, does not establish whether you are eligible for transfer. I don’t know your school’s Medicine cut-off and I don’t know your post-UTME score. You need to check **both**, not just assume that a high JAMB score settles everything.

My own first-semester CGPA is **4.31**. I’m not coming here to pretend that I’m already at 4.5 and just waiting for my name to appear on an MBBS list. I’m below the benchmark my adviser mentioned, and I’m still pushing. It is possible to work hard and still discover that 4.5 is a serious task. That is the reality.

As for Biology 100L itself, nobody should accept it thinking it will be a soft place to relax for one year. My courses include BIO 101, CHM 101, PHY 101, MTH 101 and GST. Physics and Maths are the ones really dealing with people in my set. You have lectures, practicals, manuals, tests and all the normal university wahala. In my own school, my lab coat was ₦6,500, my dissecting kit was ₦9,000, and the practical manual was separate. Your own prices may differ, but I’m mentioning it because there are practical expenses and responsibilities that people don’t talk about when they just say, “Enter Biology first.”

Now, is Biology a bad course? Honestly, no. But that answer is coming from somebody who did not arrive here loving it.

The day I saw Biology on my portal, I locked myself inside my cousin’s room in Surulere and cried. I didn’t eat. It felt as if everybody was going to ask me what happened and I would have to keep explaining that I didn’t get the course I had been announcing. My mum was still telling people in church that I was studying Medicine for about two months. I eventually had to beg her to stop because correcting people again and again was making everything worse.

So when you say you’ve been crying since afternoon, I understand. Don’t let anybody make you feel childish for grieving something you really wanted.

But something unexpected happened when I started the course. During our first BIO practical, we dissected toads. One guy in my group actually fainted. I was fine, and I found myself genuinely interested in what we were doing. That was the day it first occurred to me that maybe I actually liked this thing, not just that I was managing it because I had no choice. Now I’m enjoying genetics and cell biology much more than I expected.

That does not mean I woke up and forgot Medicine completely. It just means Biology stopped looking like punishment to me. It is a real course with things you can genuinely become interested in, not a waiting room where everybody is automatically miserable until they escape to MBBS.

Still, I won’t use my experience to convince you that you will feel the same way. You may start Biology and discover you love it. You may also confirm that what you really want is Medicine. Both are valid things to learn about yourself.

On rewriting, please don’t let anybody romanticise staying at home. My secondary school classmate Ifeoma rejected a Pharmacy offer because she wanted to rewrite for Medicine. She has written JAMB two more times since then and she is still at home. I’m not mentioning her to frighten you or suggest that everybody who rewrites fails. Rewriting can work. But there is also no guarantee that one more JAMB automatically produces Medicine, and people rarely discuss the emotional side of watching your mates resume while you are preparing for another exam.

At the same time, staying at home being difficult does not mean you must accept any admission at all costs. If you know in your heart that you do not want a Biology degree and Medicine is what you are fully prepared to pursue again, rewriting is not wrong. Just make that decision with your eyes open, not because somebody commented “one year is nothing” under your post.

Since your acceptance-fee deadline is in two weeks, please don’t spend the whole two weeks going back and forth with forum people. Go to your own faculty or department, or call the appropriate official office if you cannot go physically. Ask to speak to a level adviser or whoever handles transfers, and ask them directly:

- Does your school actually allow movement from Biology to MBBS after 100L?
- What exact CGPA is required?
- Does space have to be available, and how are people selected when applicants are more than the spaces?
- Must you have met Medicine’s JAMB and post-UTME cut-offs when you first applied?
- With your exact scores, would you even be eligible to compete for transfer?
- How many people, if any, were moved in recent years?

Please don’t just trust forum people, **including me**. Everything I’ve said about requirements is what my own adviser told us about my own school. Your university may be completely different.

Then sit down and ask yourself one honest question: do you want Medicine itself, or do you mainly want to be “doctor” because that is what your parents and everybody around you have been expecting? Family pressure is real, and wanting to make your parents proud is not a crime. But you are the person who will attend the classes, write the exams and live with the outcome, so your own answer matters.

My honest advice is this: **don’t accept Biology solely because somebody has promised you that transfer will happen.** If you accept it, let it be with the understanding that you may finish in Biology, and that Biology is still a worthwhile degree. You can pursue transfer if your school confirms that you are eligible, but don’t treat it as guaranteed. If you choose to rewrite, do it because you have considered the pressure and uncertainty and still believe it is the right route for you, not because you’re ashamed of telling people you were offered Biology.

Neither option comes with a guarantee. But neither option means your life is finished. Please eat something, rest if you can, and get the official information before making your decision. This portal result feels like it has decided your whole future right now, but it hasn’t. Whatever you choose, it is not the end of the world.
